title: Mini-simulacro 2
intro: Proporciones cercanas al blueprint 2026 (≈ 40 %): 10 huecos de Complete the Words, un set de Daily Life, un pasaje, 6 respuestas cortas, conversación, anuncio y charla, 5 Build a Sentence, email, discusión, 7 Listen and Repeat y 2 preguntas de entrevista.

items.q: Completa las palabras (escribe solo las letras que faltan).
items.text: Tides are caused {{prima|rily}} by the {{gravita|tional}} pull of the moon, although the sun also {{contri|butes}}. As the Earth {{rota|tes}}, different coastal {{regi|ons}} pass through the bulges of water created by this {{attra|ction}}, {{resul|ting}} in two high tides and two low tides each day. The height of the tides varies {{consid|erably}} depending on the shape of the {{shore|line}} and the depth of the {{surrou|nding}} sea.

blocks.title: Read in Daily Life
blocks.passage:
GREENFIELD FITNESS CENTER — Winter Schedule (Dec 1 – Feb 28)

Weekdays: 6:30 a.m. – 10:00 p.m.
Saturdays: 8:00 a.m. – 6:00 p.m.
Sundays and public holidays: closed

Group classes (yoga, spinning, circuit training) require booking through the app up to 48 hours in advance. Bookings can be cancelled free of charge until 3 hours before the class; later cancellations count as attended.

New members receive one complimentary personal training session. Lockers must be emptied nightly; items left overnight will be removed.

items.explain: «Sundays and public holidays: closed».

items.explain: «later cancellations count as attended» (el límite es 3 horas antes).

blocks.title: Read an Academic Passage
blocks.passage:
When farmland is abandoned, nature does not simply return to its former state. Ecologists studying such "rewilded" landscapes in Europe have found that the pace and direction of recovery depend heavily on what animals remain nearby. Where large grazers such as wild horses or bison are reintroduced, the grass stays short and open habitats persist, which benefits insects and ground-nesting birds. Without grazers, shrubs quickly dominate and eventually form dense woodland.

Neither outcome is inherently better; each supports different species. Consequently, conservationists increasingly regard rewilding not as a single formula but as a set of choices that should reflect local goals. Critics worry that unmanaged landscapes may increase wildfire risk or conflict with farmers, though supporters respond that carefully planned grazing can reduce both concerns.

items.q: What is the passage mainly about?
options: How rewilded land develops and why management choices matter
items.explain: Desarrolla cómo evoluciona la tierra y por qué las decisiones importan.

items.q: According to the passage, what happens where large grazers are absent?
options: Shrubs soon dominate and woodland forms
items.explain: «Without grazers, shrubs quickly dominate and eventually form dense woodland».

items.q: The word "inherently" is closest in meaning to
items.explain: inherently = por naturaleza.

items.q: Why does the author mention critics in paragraph 2?
options: To show that the approach has concerns that supporters answer
items.explain: Presenta una objeción y la respuesta de los partidarios.

items.q: What can be inferred about the author's view of rewilding?
options: It should follow one fixed method
Its results depend on local goals and choices
It is dangerous and should stop
items.explain: Presenta el rewilding como «a set of choices that should reflect local goals».

segments.text: Good morning, everyone. A quick announcement before we begin. Tomorrow's chemistry lab has been moved from Room 204 to Room 118, because the ventilation system in 204 is being repaired. Please bring your safety goggles and a printed copy of the procedure, as the printers in the new room are out of order. Also, the quiz scheduled for Thursday will cover only the first two units, not the third, as previously stated.

items.q: Why has the lab been moved?
options: The ventilation system is being repaired
items.explain: «the ventilation system in 204 is being repaired».

items.q: What should students bring?
options: Safety goggles and a printed procedure
items.explain: «safety goggles and a printed copy of the procedure».

items.q: What has changed about the quiz?
options: It will cover only two units
items.explain: «will cover only the first two units, not the third».

segments.text: Let's talk about the placebo effect, which occurs when a patient improves after receiving a treatment that contains no active ingredient. Researchers once assumed this was just imagination, but brain scans suggest otherwise. When patients expect pain relief, their brains release natural painkillers called endorphins.

Interestingly, the effect depends on presentation. In one study, patients received identical sugar pills, but those told they were expensive reported greater relief than those told they were cheap. Even more surprising, some patients improved when they were told honestly that the pills were placebos.

What does this mean for medicine? Doctors cannot simply prescribe placebos, because that would involve deception. However, they can improve outcomes by communicating clearly and showing empathy, since expectations shape the body's response.

items.q: What is the main point of the talk?
options: Expectations can produce real physiological effects
items.explain: Expectativas → endorfinas → alivio real.

items.q: What did brain scans suggest?
items.explain: «their brains release natural painkillers called endorphins».

items.q: Why does the professor describe the study with expensive and cheap pills?
options: To show the effect depends on presentation
items.explain: Es evidencia de que la presentación modifica el efecto.

items.q: What would the professor most likely advise doctors?
items.explain: Conclusión final.

blocks.title: Write an Email
blocks.prompt:
**Situation.** You ordered a textbook from the university bookstore two weeks ago, but it has not arrived, and the exam is next week.

**Write an email to the bookstore manager.** In your email:
- Describe the problem and your order.
- Explain why you need the book soon.
- Ask for a specific solution.
blocks.model:
Dear Bookstore Manager,

I am writing about an order I placed on October 14 for the textbook Principles of Thermodynamics (order number 5521). Although I was told it would arrive within five days, I have not received it after two weeks.

I urgently need the book because I have an exam next Thursday, and no copies are available in the library. Could you please let me know where my order is and, if it cannot arrive before Tuesday, arrange for me to pick up a copy from another branch or receive a refund?

Thank you for your prompt attention.

Sincerely,
Marta Silva

blocks.title: Write for an Academic Discussion
blocks.prompt:
**Professor Silva:** Some universities now provide free meals to all students. Is this a worthwhile use of resources?

**Ahmed:** Absolutely. Hungry students cannot concentrate, so free meals improve learning.

**Grace:** I disagree. Funds should go to teaching and research, and students who can pay should do so.

**Write a response** (≥ 100 words) giving your opinion with a reason and an example, and refer to Ahmed or Grace.
blocks.model:
I partly agree with Ahmed. Hunger does reduce concentration, and I have seen classmates skip meals during exams because they were short of money. Free meals for students who need them could therefore improve results.

However, Grace is right that resources are limited. A universal program would also feed students who can easily pay. A better option would be to offer free or subsidized meals based on need, as several Dutch universities do with meal vouchers.

In this way, the university would support learning while keeping money for teaching and research.

questions.q: What advice would you give to a student who has trouble managing time?
questions.model: I would suggest planning each week in advance and breaking big tasks into small steps. For example, I use a calendar with fixed study blocks, and that has stopped me from leaving work for the last minute.

questions.q: Do you think it is better to read the news every day or to focus only on topics you study?
questions.model: I think a balance is best. Reading the news broadens your perspective, but your studies need deep focus. For instance, I read the headlines in the morning and then concentrate on my courses.
